chunks: What the Shaykh—may Allah Most High support him—informed me of, from Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, from Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from ʿAlī ibn Ismāʿīl, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ḥarīz, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a dog touching something from the body of a human being. He said: “The place that it touched should be washed.”

key_terms.أَصَابَهُ: it touched or reached it, referring to the dog's contact with the body
key_terms.الْكَلْبِ: the dog, the source of the contact discussed in the ruling
key_terms.الْمَكَانُ: the place or area, meaning the specific spot touched
key_terms.جَسَدِ الْإِنْسَانِ: the human body, the object affected by the contact
key_terms.يُغْسَلُ: it should be washed, indicating the required act of purification

ai.seo_question: What should be done if a dog touches part of a person's body according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on ritual purity concerning contact of a dog with the human body. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام states that the affected area is to be washed, indicating the purification required for such contact in fiqh.
